conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that arthroscopy does not meaningfully help knee osteoarthritis, citing landmark randomized trials showing outcomes are no better than placebo or non-surgical care, and major guidelines strongly recommending against its use.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion: No—arthroscopy does not meaningfully help osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee when used to wash out or “clean up” the arthritic joint (lavage/debridement).**

**Why the answer is no:**  
- A landmark placebo-controlled randomized trial found that outcomes after arthroscopic lavage or debridement were **no better than placebo surgery**. This is especially persuasive because it controls for the effects of undergoing an operation and expecting benefit.  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12110735/  
- A later randomized trial in people with **moderate-to-severe knee OA** compared arthroscopy plus optimized physical/medical treatment against optimized non-surgical treatment alone—testing whether surgery adds value to good conservative care.  
  https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa0708333  
- Systematic-review evidence, which pools randomized trials, evaluates both benefits (pain/function) and harms of arthroscopic surgery for degenerative knee disease (OA, often with degenerative meniscal tears). The 2022 Cochrane update notes that major guidelines strongly recommend against its use.  
  https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD014328_arthroscopic-surgery-degenerative-knee-disease  

**Important nuance:** arthroscopy may still be considered to treat a *separate mechanical problem*—for example, a loose body causing a clear, true locking episode—not to treat OA itself. UK guidance says it should not be offered as OA treatment except where there is a clear history of mechanical locking.  
https://ebi.aomrc.org.uk/interventions/knee-arthroscopy-for-patients-with-osteoarthritis/  

Thus, subjective improvement after arthroscopy can occur, but trials show it is not a reliable treatment effect beyond placebo or appropriate non-operative care, and it does not reverse OA.
